# OpenTDCR

A release candidate for tendon-driven continuum robot hardware and simple Python teleoperation, from the Continuum Robotics Lab, University of Toronto.

- [Getting started](guide.html): package install, dry-run, hardware and sensor interface.
- [Release status](release-notes.html): verified contents, missing hardware information and licensing status.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/ContinuumRoboticsLab/OpenTDCR): clean source with README, AGENTS.md, docs, tests, CAD, and examples.
- [Research project](https://continuumroboticslab.github.io/opencr-mujoco/): companion paper and original physics demo.

The webpage has an automatically moving, illustrative constant-curvature backbone with three optional draggable Clarke-coordinate pads. The scroll-driven CAD view lays out 26 component groups, including sixteen spools extracted from disconnected solids in the original servo mesh. Printed plates and spools sit at the front; the motor bank sits to the side. All original CAD triangles are preserved. The flexible backbone is absent from that CAD. A separate scroll story illustrates input, coordinates, tendon motion, and tip motion. The generalized Clarke mapping cycles through 3, 4, 6, and 8 equally spaced tendons. Haptic input is an adapter-extension concept; the released input paths are keyboard and wired DualSense. Both views are explanatory visualizations, not physics simulation. The package defaults to dry run; never enable physical motors without explicit user authorization and reviewed device configuration. Hardware licensing and bench validation remain pending. Source archive contains no internal project Git history or lab recordings.

Clarke coordinate reference: Grassmann and Burgner-Kahrs (2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12265. Source repository: https://github.com/ContinuumRoboticsLab/OpenTDCR. Project webpage: https://continuumroboticslab.github.io/OpenTDCR/.

Calibration: `tdcr calibrate` preserves the loosen, measured-tip threshold, countback, common adjustment, and reference-capture sequence. Thresholds and countbacks are configurable; sensors implement a generic measurement contract, with Lyra as an optional adapter. Default calibration runs use synthetic measurements. See repository docs/calibration.md. Acknowledgement: Kyum Lee, Chengnan Shentu, Chloe Pogue, Jessica Burgner-Kahrs, ICRA 2025, https://doi.org/10.1109/ICRA55743.2025.11128689.
